comment: Leak-scan rules for tools/publish.ps1. Hitting a DENY rule blocks the push.
This file is public on purpose: the patterns are generic and documenting them
makes the sanitization guarantee auditable. Machine-specific literal secrets
(account names, LAN IPs, hostnames) must NOT be listed here -- they live in

deny.hint: Absolute Windows user path. Replace with a placeholder like <DSH_HOME> / <WORKSPACE>, or derive it at runtime from $env:USERPROFILE / os.homedir().
Absolute home path. Same treatment as windows-user-path.
Private/LAN IP address. Replace with <LAN_IP>. If it is a documentation example, use an RFC 5737 address (192.0.2.x / 198.51.100.x / 203.0.113.x).
A GitHub token literal. NEVER publish one. Also rotate it if it was ever committed.
Looks like an API key literal.
Looks like an AWS access key id.

warn.hint: Email address. Fine if it is a doc placeholder (you@example.com); otherwise strip it.
Looks like a hard-coded secret assignment. Usually a doc example, but check it.
Possible personal name attached to a role. Keep the repo free of identity. (Anchored to end-of-line on purpose: code like `$owner = Get-Foo` is not a name.)
